author: Unsigned statement (corpus lists General Conference of SDA)
work: Fundamental Principles of Seventh-day Adventists, 1889 Year Book, p. 147, preamble
text: As elsewhere stated, Seventh-day Adventists have no creed but the Bible; but they hold to certain well-defined points of faith, for which they feel prepared to give a reason “to every man that asketh” them. The following propositions may be taken as a summary of the principal features of their religious faith, upon which there is, so far as we know, entire unanimity throughout the body.
note: 1889 preamble: Seventh-day Adventists “have no creed but the Bible”; the propositions are “a summary of the principal features of their religious faith.”

author: Unsigned statement (corpus lists General Conference of SDA)
work: Fundamental Principles of Seventh-day Adventists, 1889 Year Book, p. 148, Principle III
text: III. That the Holy Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments were given by inspiration of God, contain a full revelation of his will to man, and are the only infallible rule of faith and practice.
note: Principle III: the Scriptures of both Testaments were “given by inspiration of God,” “contain a full revelation of his will to man,” and are “the only infallible rule of faith and practice.”

author: Unsigned statement (corpus lists General Conference of SDA)
work: A Declaration of the Fundamental Principles Taught and Practiced by the Seventh-day Adventists (Battle Creek: SDA Publishing Association, 1872), preface
text: In presenting to the public this synopsis of our faith, we wish to have it distinctly understood that we have no articles of faith, creed, or discipline, aside from the Bible. We do not put forth this as having any authority with our people, nor is it designed to secure uniformity among them, as a system of faith, but is a brief statement of what is, and has been, with great unanimity, held by them.
note: 1872 preface: “no articles of faith, creed, or discipline, aside from the Bible”; the synopsis is not put forth “as having any authority with our people.”

author: James White (unsigned editorial section introducing Ellen White’s vision; the corpus lists the pamphlet under James White)
text: The bible is a perfect, and complete revelation. It is our only rule of faith and practice. But this is no reason, why God may not show the past, present, and future fulfilment of his word, in these last days, by dreams and visions; according to Peter’s testimony. True visions are given to lead us to God, and his written word; but those that are given for a new rule of faith and practice, separate from the bible, cannot be from God, and should be rejected.
note: 1847: the Bible is “our only rule of faith and practice”; “True visions are given to lead us to God, and his written word,” and visions given as “a new rule of faith and practice, separate from the bible” are to be rejected.

author: J. N. Loughborough (speech as reported in the conference minutes; U. Smith, secretary)
work: “Doings of the Battle Creek Conference, Oct. 5 & 6, 1861,” Advent Review and Sabbath Herald, October 8, 1861
text: The first step of apostasy is to get up a creed, telling us what we shall believe. The second is, to make that creed a test of fellowship. The third is to try members by that creed. The fourth to denounce as heretics those who do not believe that creed. And, fifth, to commence persecution against such.
note: Loughborough, 1861 (in the debate on a church covenant): “The first step of apostasy is to get up a creed”; the later steps make it a test of fellowship and end in persecution.

author: James White (speech as reported in the conference minutes)
work: “Doings of the Battle Creek Conference, Oct. 5 & 6, 1861,” Advent Review and Sabbath Herald, October 8, 1861
text: Now I take the ground that creeds stand in direct opposition to the gifts. … The Bible is our creed. We reject everything in the form of a human creed. We take the Bible and the gifts of the Spirit; embracing the faith that thus the Lord will teach us from time to time.
note: James White, 1861: “The Bible is our creed”; creeds “stand in direct opposition to the gifts,” and Adventists “take the Bible and the gifts of the Spirit.”

author: Ellen G. White
work: The Spirit of Prophecy, vol. 4 (1884); the same passage stands in The Great Controversy (GC 595.1)
text: But God will have a people upon the earth to maintain the Bible, and the Bible only, as the standard of all doctrines and the basis of all reforms. The opinions of learned men, the deductions of science, the creeds or decisions of ecclesiastical councils, as numerous and discordant as are the churches which they represent, the voice of the majority,—not one or all of these should be regarded as evidence for or against any point of religious faith. Before accepting any doctrine or precept, we should demand a plain “Thus saith the Lord” in its support.
note: EGW, 1884: “the Bible, and the Bible only, as the standard of all doctrines”; creeds, councils, science and majorities are not “evidence for or against any point of religious faith.”

author: Uriah Smith
work: Replies to Elder Canright’s Attacks on Seventh-day Adventists (1887)
text: We stand on the great Protestant platform that “the Bible and the Bible alone” is our rule of faith and practice. … We believe that God by his grace and his providence has given existence to the book we call “the Bible” as a revelation of his will to man; that holy men wrote it, as God spoke to them face to face, or moved upon them by the Holy Spirit, or revealed truths to them in visions or dreams, … that this volume is complete in itself, and is to have nothing taken from it nor added to it; and that this is set forth as the standard and test of all moral teaching, all spiritual exercises, and all revelation purporting to be either human or divine.
note: Uriah Smith, 1887: “the Bible and the Bible alone” is the rule; “holy men wrote it”; it is “complete in itself” and the “standard and test” of “all revelation purporting to be either human or divine” (answering the charge that the visions are set above the Bible, RCASDA 75.3).
